note: Window agent p1910-p1919, 2 Nov 2026. Six entries: the Republic of China's three southern provinces back in July 1916, the Ukrainian State's governorates at the end of 1918, Ruanda-Urundi in 1917-1918, Tuva in 1914, the Mosul vilayet from November 1918, and southern Mozambique held in the Republic's own name. Angola's equivalent (about 2,000 cells held by portuguese-republic) is not patched: the colony's own keyframes of 1912 and 1915 release any cell added by an event, so it needs a dossier fix. Review 2 Nov 2026: events/2 changed from occupation_start to gain with keyframe_overrides/1 added (the occupation broke Iraq in 1922-1931); events/3 moved to January 1910. Seam sm-06, 3 Nov 2026: events/4 (the northern Lado land stays with the Sudan in 1914) and events/5 (Darfur to the Sudan in 1917) added. Review sm-06, 3 Nov 2026: the notes of events/4 and events/5 now open with a dated caption sentence (the compile shows a note's first sentence as the map caption).

region.text: the Kiev, Chernigov, Poltava, Kharkov, Yekaterinoslav, Taurida (mainland) and Volhynia governorates that the Ukrainian State administered: Kyiv, Chernihiv, Sumy, Poltava, Kharkiv, Dnipropetrovsk, Zaporizhzhya and Zhytomyr oblasts

events.note: 1918, spring: after the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk 'German forces then recaptured much of the Ukrainian territory under the control of the Bolsheviks, including Kyiv itself', and the Ukrainian State (established 29 April 1918, 'Client state of the German Empire') governed the Kiev, Chernigov, Kharkov, Poltava, Yekaterinoslav, Volhynia and Podolia governorates. The ukrainian-soviet-socialist-republic ledger hands the land it lost in March and April to the Central Powers (german-empire), and the German keyframe of 1918 then releases it to nobody, leaving about 670 Ukrainian cells with no owner at the end of 1918 although the Hetmanate held them until the Directorate took over in December. The land goes to the Ukrainian State, a vassal of the Empire until November.

region.text: Tannu Uriankhai, largely the modern Tuva

events.note: April 1914: 'In April 1914 Tannu Uriankhai was formally accepted as a protectorate of Russia.' The Uryankhay republic dissolves in 1914 and its land goes to nobody until the Russian keyframe of 1915 takes it back, so Tuva is unowned at the end of 1914; the land passes to the Empire in April.

region.text: the Mosul vilayet: Ninawa, Dahuk, Arbil, Kirkuk (At-Ta'mim) and Sulaymaniyah

events.note: 14 November 1918: after the Armistice of Mudros (30 October 1918) Cobbe 'continued to advance on Mosul in the face of Turkish protests' and 'British troops marched unopposed into the city on the 14 November 1918'; 'The ownership of Mosul Province and its rich oil fields became an international issue'. The province passes to the Empire as the dossier's own gain of 14 November 1918 passes the rest of Iraq; without this the Ottoman keyframe of 1919 drops it to nobody. [Review 2 Nov 2026: was occupation_start. An Ottoman-owned Mosul passed straight to kingdom-of-iraq at its founding in August 1921 and turned the roles of the British occupation event of that month, so the trial of p1920-p1929 left 748 cells of central and southern Iraq to nobody from 1922 to 1931. As a gain it needs keyframe_overrides/1, which keeps the province in the British 1918-1919 shape.]

region.text: Mozambique, 'extending from Lourenço Marques in the south to Niassa in the north'

events.note: 1910: Mozambique is a 'Territory of the Portuguese Empire (1505-1951)', the 'Province of Mozambique (1893-1926)', 'extending from Lourenço Marques in the south to Niassa in the north'. About 250 southern cells are held by portuguese-empire in its own name on 1 January 1910 and pass to the Republic through its 1910 keyframe, drawn in the Republic's colour inside the colony; they belong to the colony (data/colonies.csv: portuguese-mozambique, metropole portuguese-empire to 1910, portuguese-republic from 1911). [Review 2 Nov 2026: moved from January 1911 (counterpart portuguese-republic) to January 1910 (counterpart portuguese-empire), so that the end of 1910 is right too.]

region.text: the part of the Lado Enclave that lies inside modern South Sudan, the northern half that stayed in the Sudan

events.note: 1 January 1914: in the exchange with Uganda only 'a southern part of the enclave' goes to Uganda (it 'was renamed West Nile'); the northern half of the Lado Enclave stays in the Sudan. The Sudan's ledger row of 1 January 1914 (ledger/6, the exchange with Uganda) is written over the whole 'Lado Enclave' region, so the draft handed all 109 northern Lado cells to british-africa from 1914. The page dates two cessions only: 'In 1912 the southern half of the Lado Enclave was ceded to Uganda' and 'on 1 January 1914 Sudan formally exchanged part of the enclave for a stretch of the Upper Nile'; the land that went to Uganda 'was renamed West Nile', so the northern half stays Sudanese (the dossier's keyframe of 1912 says 'its northern half inside the South Sudan outline'). The page does not say which cells the 1914 exchange moved; this keeps the cells inside today's South Sudan with the Sudan, as the keyframe of 1916 (the whole of South Sudan) does from 1916.

region.text: Darfur, the former sultanate of Ali Dinar

events.note: 1917: Darfur, conquered in 1916, is incorporated into the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan ('The kingdom was incorporated into the Anglo-Egyptian Condominium in 1917', Sultanate of Darfur page). In 1916 british-africa/ledger/35 and the sultanate's own dissolution (6 November 1916, counterpart british-africa) put all of Darfur (1,811 cells) with british-africa, and because those events moved the cells in 1916 they outrank the Sudan's keyframe of 1916 (which now resolves), so the draft kept Darfur under british-africa to the end of 1929. This gives it to the Sudan in 1917.

minus.text: Tibet's land as the tibet dossier draws it: U-Tsang, Chamdo and Kham west of the Yangtze, with the Tawang tract

correction.text: the 1916 outline with Yunnan, Guizhou and Guangxi back in the Republic (the ledger gain of 14 July 1916); without Tibet's land, which the Republic claimed but did not govern

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's 1916 keyframe is the March-July state without Yunnan, Guizhou and Guangxi, but the compiler checks it at the end of 1916, after the ledger gain of July. 'Eight days after his death, on 14 July 1916, the National Protection War was ended' with the provinces 'rescinding their declarations of independence', so at the end of 1916 the three provinces (about 2,990 cells) sat unowned until the 1917 keyframe. The corrected shape keeps them in the Republic.

correction.text: Cliopatria shape of 1918 minus all of Canada except Newfoundland and Labrador, which stay a separate British colony; New Zealand; Kuwait; without the German New Guinea land that Cliopatria adds to the British shape from 1915; without the Indonesian cells of Cliopatria's shape; with the Mosul vilayet (Ninawa, Dahuk, Arbil, Kirkuk and Sulaymaniyah), entered on 14 November 1918

keyframe_overrides.why: Added by the reviewer with events/2. The dossier's own correction is kept unchanged; its note dates the Mosul entry to 14 November 1918 ('British troops marched unopposed into the city on the 14 November 1918') but Cliopatria's British shape adds the Mosul cells only in 1920, so the 1918 snap would release the province that events/2 gives to the Empire. The union adds 309 cells, all inside the five Mosul governorates, and removes none.

region.text: Rwanda and Burundi, the Belgian-occupied Ruanda-Urundi

rulings.why: 'Ruanda was occupied over April-May and Urundi in June 1916' and the land 'was administered by Belgium under military occupation from 1916 to 1922' (Royal Commissioner from February 1917). The size rule gave Rwanda and Burundi to ruanda-urundi in 1917 but back to german-africa in 1918 (the Cliopatria shape of German Africa), which the page does not support.
